new_candidates.body:
## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04
- Source: `gazebosim/gz-physics` `main` at `b44cd0d` (also seen on `4e2af8c`; `Base.cc` is unchanged between them)
- MuJoCo 3.11.0, as pinned in `third_party/mujoco_vendor/CMakeLists.txt` (`b85fdca54f0e0038b804af146a0b4e94199e00d0`)

## Description

Expected behavior: a joint added to a world that was already compiled starts with a zero control, like the ones of the initial compilation.

Actual behavior: the first step after adding the model reports `Nan, Inf or huge value in CTRL`, or the joint receives a random force.

Cause: `Base::RecompileSpec` calls `mj_recompile`, which calls `mjCModel::SaveState`. In MuJoCo 3.11.0 that function saves `ctrl[i]` for every actuator of the spec (`src/user/user_model.cc` L4289 at tag 3.11.0), including the actuators added since the last compilation. Their index is past the end of the old `mjData::ctrl` array (`nu` of the old model), so the read is out of bounds. The new actuators start with whatever memory follows `ctrl`: the padding before `qfrc_applied`, or `qfrc_applied` itself.

MuJoCo fixed this in 3.14.0 (commit `c7967ce`, "Preserve full integration state and control blocks in mj_recompile"): `SaveState` indexes the controls by `ctrladr_` and skips actuators that have none yet (the new ones). 3.13.0 still has the bug. The plugin pins 3.11.0, so it needs a workaround until the vendored MuJoCo is bumped (a branch `jrivero/mujoco_3_17_0_update` exists).

Source (3.11.0): https://github.com/google-deepmind/mujoco/blob/3.11.0/src/user/user_model.cc#L4289

## Steps to reproduce

We saw it in gz-sim, with models spawned after the world started. The same sequence with the plugin only:

1. Construct an empty world, add a model with one revolute joint, and set a force on the joint (this compiles the world: `nu` is 1).
2. Add a second model with a revolute joint.
3. Read a joint position (this recompiles the world: `nu` is 2) and look at `mjData::ctrl[1]` and `mjData::warning[mjWARN_BADCTRL]`. If the memory after `ctrl` holds a huge value, `ctrl[1]` holds it too and the warning counter increases.

The test in the proposed fix does exactly this, filling the memory after `ctrl` with `1e30` first so that the result does not depend on what the allocator left there.

## Output

With the test of the proposed fix and the fix reverted (MuJoCo 3.11.0, same result in three runs):

```text
WARNING: Nan, Inf or huge value in CTRL at ACTUATOR 1. The simulation is unstable. Time = 0.0000.

RecompileSpec_TEST.cc:169: Failure
Expected equality of these values:
  0.0
  d->ctrl[1]
    Which is: 1e+30
RecompileSpec_TEST.cc:171: Failure
  0
  d->warning[mjWARN_BADCTRL].number
    Which is: 1
RecompileSpec_TEST.cc:178: Failure
  0
  worldInfo->mjDataObj->warning[mjWARN_BADCTRL].number
    Which is: 2
```

A fix is proposed in the PR that references this issue: zero the controls of the actuators beyond the old `nu` after the recompilation. It does nothing on MuJoCo 3.14.0 and later.
new_candidates.title: MuJoCo: actuators added after the first compilation start with garbage controls (mj_recompile out-of-bounds read)

new_candidates.body:
## Environment
* OS Version: Ubuntu 24.04
* Source or binary build? Binary: ROS Jazzy `gz_sim_vendor`, gz-sim 8.15.0, gz-physics 7, DART engine. The tests below were built from source on `gz-sim8`.

## Description
* Expected behavior: a `LinearVelocityCmd` or `AngularVelocityCmd` set once on a model or a link changes its velocity once, and then the entity moves freely, as on gz-sim 9 and later (#2228).
* Actual behavior: after each step the Physics system sets both components to zero but keeps them, so the following steps apply a zero command and the entity is held at zero linear and angular velocity until someone removes the component.

This is the behaviour reported in #1926. #2228 changed it on `main` (gz-sim 9) and was not backported, because it changes behaviour (Migration.md, "Gazebo Sim 8.x to 9.0").

We run Harmonic for a legged robot simulation, where a velocity set once is lost after one step: `ros_gz_sim` `SetEntityState` with a twist, and resetting a world to a state with a velocity. A system that sets the command every step is not affected.

## Question
Would a change of this behaviour be acceptable on `gz-sim8`, limited to the model and link commands (`LinearVelocityCmd`, `AngularVelocityCmd`)? `JointVelocityCmd` would keep being zeroed, because gz-sim 8's `MulticopterMotorModel` relies on the component existing. If not, we keep carrying the patch downstream and no PR is needed. #3696 notes that removing the components every step also costs systems that set them continuously (change detection, scene broadcaster), so we would like your view before opening a PR.

## Prepared change
https://github.com/facontidavide/gz-sim/tree/backport/2228-remove-velocity-cmds-gz-sim8 (one commit on `gz-sim8`): the model and link part of #2228, the TrajectoryFollower hunk of #2228 that depends on it, a Migration.md entry, and two tests in `INTEGRATION_physics_system`, `ModelVelocityCmdAppliedOnce` and `LinkVelocityCmdAppliedOnce`. Each sets a linear and an angular velocity command once on the falling sphere of `falling.sdf`, runs 200 steps, and checks that no command component is left after any step and that x and yaw advance at the commanded rate.

## Output
Built from source on `gz-sim8` (Ubuntu 24.04, ROS Jazzy vendor dependencies):

| | `INTEGRATION_physics_system` | the two new tests |
|---|---|---|
| unmodified `gz-sim8` | passes | (not present) |
| with the change | passes | pass |
| change reverted, tests kept | fails | fail: a command component is left after all 200 of 200 steps (expected 0), and the x and yaw checks fail |

`INTEGRATION_velocity_control_system`, `INTEGRATION_multicopter`, `INTEGRATION_odometry_publisher`, `INTEGRATION_link`, `INTEGRATION_model` and `UNIT_AddedMass_TEST` pass with the change. `INTEGRATION_tracked_vehicle_system` fails in our environment with and without the change, also on unmodified `gz-sim8`.
new_candidates.title: gz-sim8: model and link velocity commands are zeroed, not removed, after each step (backport of #2228?)

new_candidates.body:
## Feature request

When the robot is moving, a global plan starts from the pose at which the planning request was sent. If planning takes time, the robot may already have moved past the start of the returned path.

I’d like to explore a reusable subtree that uses the current path and odometry to select a start pose ahead of the robot. The lookahead distance would be forward_velocity * lookahead_time. If the retained prefix of the current path is valid, the subtree would plan from its endpoint and concatenate the prefix and new plan. Otherwise, it would fall back to planning from the current pose.

This should also reduce the chance that a robot re-plans in the opposite direction from the original plan, and reduce a bit path jumps for the local planner.

#### Implementation considerations

Example BT:

```
<BehaviorTree ID="PlanWithLookahead">
  <Fallback name="PlanFromLookaheadOrCurrentPose">
    <Sequence name="PlanFromLookahead">
      <!-- New action: read fresh forward velocity from odometry -->
      <GetForwardVelocity velocity="{_velocity}"/>

      <Script code="_distance := _velocity * lookahead_time"/>
      <ScriptCondition code="_distance > 0.0"/>

      <TruncatePathLocal input_path="{path}"
                         output_path="{_prefix}"
                         distance_backward="0.0"
                         distance_forward="{_distance}"/>

      <GetPoseFromPath path="{_prefix}"
                       index="-1"
                       pose="{_start}"/>

      <ValidatePath path="{_prefix}"/>

      <ComputePathToPose start="{_start}"
                         goal="{goal}"
                         planner_id="{planner_id}"
                         path="{_suffix}"
                         error_code_id="{_lookahead_error_code}"
                         error_msg="{_lookahead_error_msg}"/>

      <ConcatenatePaths input_path1="{_prefix}"
                        input_path2="{_suffix}"
                        output_path="{path}"/>
    </Sequence>

    <ComputePathToPose goal="{goal}"
                       planner_id="{planner_id}"
                       path="{path}"
                       error_code_id="{error_code}"
                       error_msg="{error_msg}"/>
  </Fallback>
</BehaviorTree>
```
new_candidates.title: Support lookahead-start replanning with a behavior subtree

new_candidates.body:
## Feature request

Nav2’s periodic replanning can replace a valid path even when the new path offers little improvement (and possibly a different start-direction) or takes a much longer detour around a temporary obstacle. This can cause unnecessary route changes and less predictable navigation.

A selective replanning behavior could combine periodic planning with mandatory replanning when the goal changes, the robot deviates too far from the path, or a collision persists for a configured duration. Mandatory replans would apply a usable result directly. Periodic candidates would be applied only when:
- A longer detour has persisted for a configured duration; or
- A non-detour candidate improves a score based on path length and length-normalized cost by a configurable minimum.
Keeping the candidate separate from the active path would let the controller continue following the accepted path while planning and evaluation run.

Pausing on blocked path, as described in https://github.com/ros-navigation/navigation2/issues/2877, could also be optional part of the strategy.

#### Implementation considerations

The tree could be structured as follows. ObserveReplanningTriggers, ReplanWhenRequested, and SelectCandidate are proposed reusable components:

```
<PipelineSequence name="NavigateWithSelectiveReplanning">

  <SubTree ID="ObserveReplanningTriggers"
           goal="{goal}"
           active_path="{active_path}"
           active_path_revision="{active_path_revision}"
           tracking_feedback="{tracking_feedback}"
           mandatory_replan="{mandatory_replan}"/>

  <ReplanWhenRequested trigger="{mandatory_replan}"
                       goal="{goal}"
                       periodic_hz="0.5"
                       planning_goal="{planning_goal}"
                       mandatory_request="{mandatory_request}">

    <Sequence name="ComputeSelectAndApply">
      <ComputePathToPose goal="{planning_goal}"
                         path="{candidate_path}"
                         planner_id="{selected_planner}"/>

      <SubTree ID="SelectCandidate"
               mandatory="{mandatory_request}"
               goal="{planning_goal}"
               active_path="{active_path}"
               active_path_revision="{active_path_revision}"
               candidate_path="{candidate_path}"
               accept_candidate="{accept_candidate}"/>

      <Script _skipIf="!accept_candidate"
              code="active_path = candidate_path;
                    active_path_revision += 1"/>
    </Sequence>
  </ReplanWhenRequested>

  <FollowPath path="{active_path}"
              controller_id="{selected_controller}"
              tracking_feedback="{tracking_feedback}"/>

</PipelineSequence>
```
SelectCandidate would prune both paths at the current robot pose before comparison. The scheduler would latch whether each request is mandatory and discard results for superseded goals. Recovery behavior and parameters are omitted from the example.
new_candidates.title: Selective replanning with path acceptance policies
